title: Public Speaking and Presenting an Argument
subject: language

sections.body: Structure: open with a hook (question, story or surprising fact), state your main point, give 2–3 supporting points with evidence, and end with a strong conclusion.
Delivery: speak slower than feels natural, pause after key points, make eye contact, and use notes with key words, not a full script.
Nerves are normal. Most speakers feel them. Practise out loud, breathe slowly, and focus on your message, not yourself.

quiz.q: Which is a strong way to open a talk on plastic pollution?
options: 'By 2050, there could be more plastic than fish in the ocean by weight. So what can we do?'
'Um, so my talk is about plastic.'
'This topic is boring but here goes.'
hints: Surprising facts or questions work well.
'Did you know your heart beats about 100,000 times a day?' is a hook. Which option is similar?
quiz.explain: A surprising statistic plus a question is a strong hook. (That projection comes from a 2016 report; check the source when using it!)

quiz.q: What helps most with speaking nerves?
options: Practising out loud and breathing slowly
Reading the whole script without looking up
hints: Athletes practise before matches to feel ready. Speakers can do the same.
quiz.explain: Practice and slow breathing reduce nerves.
